opening: Thomas Hutcheson was a Glasgow legal professional and educational benefactor. Hill’s published account places his birth about 1590 and death on 1 September 1641, and names his widow Marion Stewart. These are secondary-source statements, not newly inspected originals.

position.answer: Thomas developed the school foundation after George’s hospital endowment; the inherited unmarried description and early birth estimates are corrected from attributed published evidence.
points: The existing father grade is retained; mothers and other family identities remain separately assessed.
Hill reports no issue. The printed retours name sisters as heirs in specified lands. Marion’s exact parentage remains unverified.

biography_sections.title: Career and education
biography_sections.markdown:
Thomas Hutcheson (about 1590–1641), the younger brother of George Hutcheson, was a Glasgow lawyer and educational benefactor. He was a son of Thomas Hutcheson and Helen Herbertson. George supervised his education after their father’s death. Thomas entered the University of Glasgow in 1607 and graduated in 1610. His approximate birth follows the published epitaph’s statement that he died in his fifty-second year; it is not a recovered baptism date.

He worked as a public writer and became register of sasines for the regality of Glasgow about 1627. He also acted for the University and was appointed a commissioner to visit it in 1640. Glasgow admitted him as a burgess on 24 April 1640 for his work establishing the hospital. As George’s heir and executor, Thomas ratified his brother’s charitable arrangements and used inherited wealth and property to enlarge the foundation.

Source: [ODNB public extract](https://doi.org/10.1093/ref:odnb/14276); [Hill1881](https://deriv.nls.uk/dcn23/9542/95420646.23.pdf).

biography_sections.title: Hospital and school: separate stages
biography_sections.markdown: George's deed of 16 December 1639 endowed a charitable hospital for poor older men with Trongate property and 20,000 merks. Thomas ratified the foundation in 1640 and added adjoining property and 20,200 merks for the lodging and education of twelve poor boys by his deed of 9 March 1641. Hospital here means charitable maintenance and accommodation, not a modern medical hospital. The foundation stone on 19 March 1641 and the first recorded boy's admission on 13 November 1643 are separate stages. Hill's published account says Archibald Edmiston initially attended the existing town schools; it does not show that the new foundation already taught all pupils on its own premises. Later incorporation in 1821 was not the original foundation. Sources: [Hill (1881), pp.58–63 and Appendix pp.239–252](https://archive.org/details/historyofhospita00hutc/page/58/mode/2up), [pp.203–204](https://archive.org/details/historyofhospita00hutc/page/203/mode/2up), and [the school's institutional history](https://www.hutchesons.org/our-school/our-history/). Hill's searchable published text was reviewed; manuscript deeds and admission minutes were not inspected. Conflicting published endowment totals are not silently harmonised; amounts are historical merks, with no modern purchasing-power conversion.

biography_sections.title: Widow, reported issue and succession
biography_sections.markdown:
Hill reports that Thomas died on 1 September 1641 leaving his widow, Marion Stewart, and no issue. Hill’s printed p. 47 identifies Marion as a daughter of James Stewart of Blackhall, while describing the Blackhall attribution as an inference from the tomb arms, the witnesses to a liferent charter and other manuscripts. Hill records an earlier Mynto attribution and says the marriage contract was missing. Handley also names James Stewart of Blackhall as her father and reports that she lived until November 1670. These are published accounts, and Marion’s exact parentage remains unverified. Hill’s printed p. 50 transcribes an epitaph giving the death year and age. Hill names Marion in the accompanying narrative. The original legal information, testament and monument remain uninspected. [Hill (1881), printed pp. 47 and 49–50](https://deriv.nls.uk/dcn23/9542/95420646.23.pdf), [Handley, Oxford Dictionary of National Biography](https://doi.org/10.1093/ref:odnb/14276).

The printed Lanark retours nos. 205–206, dated 24 May 1642, identify Elizabeth, Helen and Janet as Thomas’s sisters and heirs-portioners in the specified lands. This is evidence for that succession. Hill’s statement that Thomas left no issue remains a published conclusion and does not establish that Thomas never had a child. [Printed Lanark retours nos. 205–206](https://archive.org/details/inquisitionumadc00grea/page/n498/mode/1up).

On 15 October 1641 Janet, Elizabeth and Helen ratified Thomas’s hospital endowment. In the deed they describe themselves as his only lawful full sisters and heirs-portioners. [Hill, Appendix VI, pp. 254–255](https://archive.org/download/historyofhospita00hutc/page/n305.jpg).
